translations.043fdeee444901ec17105d84: Counting “it happened” → Counting “it’s correct” → Counting exceptions → Compare weeks
translations.ebac498f223087aa309e6719: Missing information → Prohibited request → Alarm situation → Did it get done right away?
translations.759330e4403af27812f8a523: Missing data is a reason to warn, never to fill in. A made-up price can look correct—and that’s exactly why it’s dangerous.
translations.c650986658b8b826774fe54a: Autonomy and supervision | Managing AI Agents · INEMA
translations.b3ddde6130a8f75c2ba50f14: Decide how much the agent can do on its own with a fixed rule, not intuition.
translations.861ac6368929250ceefa0105: Autonomy is how much the agent can do without asking for your permission. The Agent Sheet uses five steps: N0 Consults (only researches and answers), N1 Recommends (prepares drafts and suggestions), N2 Prepares, you approve (gets everything ready, but nothing leaves without your OK), N3 Executes (acts on its own and reports back) and N4 Manages processes (runs an entire process, with a report and alarms). Each step above removes you from a decision and demands more control.
translations.f37dc913e1642803a78d8bc0: The most common mistake is giving the agent the maximum step on day one, because the demo looked great. The ladder replaces the question “Do I trust the AI?” with “What evidence do I have for this step?”. It also names what you agree on with the team: “this agent is N2” says exactly what it can and can’t do.
translations.59793c950dad46fb658947a3: N0 Consults: research and answer only—doesn’t touch anything.
translations.4935f41efcd3d97ef0262b5e: N1 Recommends: prepares and suggests—the decision is yours.
translations.165b694b3691abc9095de667: N2 Prepares and you approve: nothing goes out without your explicit OK.
translations.d4dea4239d8a2eb205427cc9: N3 and N4: executes on its own or runs the process, reporting back.
translations.5af7bed5a0b2117d74c6546e: The rule starts with the action: consult becomes N0, preparation becomes N1, execution becomes N3, coordinating a process becomes N4. Then comes the brake: if the level is 3 or higher and the task involves money, something irreversible, or people from outside, the level drops to N2. Irreversible is what can’t be undone—like a sent message or a deleted file. People from outside means anyone outside the team: customer, patient, supplier, family.
translations.038c642259aa301193e161a0: These three risks are what turn a small error into losses, complaints, or a legal issue. An internal mistake you fix before anyone sees it; a wrong message sent to 200 patients doesn’t come back. That’s why it doesn’t matter how good the agent is: with any of the three, it prepares and you approve.
translations.8b8c71eeb2788713de1597bd: Money: discount, refund, charge, budget, proposal.
translations.83a1fc93f449ce8a5d48849e: People from outside: customer, patient, student, family, supplier.
translations.a895f4b366ce535d2a1ffca1: Brake: any one of the three is enough to block and keep it at N2.
translations.0bd582f50592a7ad140fc142: An official source is the place the agent must treat as truth: the system’s agenda, the orders dashboard, the discipline syllabus. The rule has a second brake: if the level is above N1 and you haven’t defined the official source, it drops to N1. Without knowing where the truth is, the agent can only suggest, never act. This applies even to internal tasks with none of the three risks.
translations.a7330f0655cbf61a975fae91: An agent without a defined source fills in the gaps with what seems plausible: an old spreadsheet, a WhatsApp message, a guess. When it only suggests, you catch the mistake before it becomes an action. When it executes, the guess becomes the wrong purchase request or false information to the customer. Defining the source is what unlocks action—not the model’s quality.
translations.76de5860fc0a4e383da391a7: Official source: the only place that counts as truth.
translations.752d423b81ca5cdaec023343: Doesn’t count: something that looks like a source, but isn’t, like an old spreadsheet.
translations.1c49be391e39c2b32550f33b: If it’s missing: warn and don’t invent.
translations.7ac6e20c3ceea03f69ae78eb: Brake: without a source, any level above N1 drops to N1.
translations.d50486744537cebd9bd3ce27: ⟪P0⟫4⟪P1⟫⟪P2⟫Prohibitions: what it never does on its own⟪P3⟫
translations.c8df9c220a44843cd0586453: Prohibitions are a short list of things the agent does not do on its own at any level, even if someone asks insistently. They work like guardrails—a protective barrier: the agent can move freely within the lane, but it doesn’t cross the wall. Each prohibition needs to come with what to say when someone requests it, so the agent can refuse without being rude and pass the case to you.
translations.7a69139b218c4bf8dcae12e4: The level says how much it can do; the prohibitions say where it never goes. Without them, a polite customer can get a discount, a student can get a grade early, and someone can get a volunteer’s phone number. And without the refusal phrase, the agent either gets stuck or improvises an excuse. Prohibitions are also the first test before you activate the agent.
translations.2770fe3965c14fa68cb4e1b6: Short list: 3 to 5 prohibitions—the ones that cost the most if they happen.
translations.bb045dfc82f1c3037adf547a: Concrete verb: “give a discount,” not “be careful with prices.”
translations.63936602e31692a087bd5358: Refusal phrase: what it says when someone asks.
translations.dbcad33336154225e26b4001: Escalate to you: every refusal becomes a note in the report.
translations.4240b99516aad0656d6df4be: The level isn’t final: it goes up when there’s evidence and comes down when there’s doubt. Promotion criteria are fixed: from N1 to N2, defined official source and 2 weeks of drafts with no major errors; from N2 to N3, 4 straight weeks approving with no need to correct anything, and only on the part of the task that doesn’t involve risk; from N3 to N4, 2 months of clean reports and working alarms. If there’s a doubt between two levels, choose the lower one.
translations.4082f65cc81be264f0ceede7: Without criteria, promotion happens from exhaustion: you stop reviewing because “it’s always right” and, without noticing, the agent turned into N3. With criteria, the increase is a decision recorded—and explained to the team. And the rule only lowers on its own: the person who raises the level is you, with proof—never the agent or urgency.
translations.be65acab7bba5dc848705e32: N1 to N2: defined official source and 2 weeks of drafts with no errors.
